item.title: Docker and Container Security Basics Every Engineering Team Underestimates | VaultRak
item.description: Containers feel isolated but are not secure by default. Running as root, pulling unverified base images, baking secrets into the image, skipping vulnerability scanning, missing a .dockerignore, and applying no resource or network limits are the six container security basics most engineering teams underestimate. VaultRak classifies Dockerfile and container configuration changes as security-relevant commits and catches these misconfigurations before they reach production. Built on Fortune 500 production expertise.
item.author: hr@t-matglobal.com (Sainath Mitalakar)

item.title: CI/CD Pipelines as a Security Surface, Not Just a Deployment Tool | VaultRak
item.description: Your CI/CD pipeline has read access to secrets, write access to your codebase, and authority to push to production. That makes it one of the highest-value attack surfaces in your infrastructure. Five vectors create the risk: secrets in environment variables, third-party actions with unreviewed code, artifact integrity gaps, overprivileged service accounts, and logs that expose sensitive runtime data. VaultRak classifies pipeline configuration changes continuously and monitors service account scope as a live posture signal. Built on Fortune 500 production expertise.
item.author: hr@t-matglobal.com (Sainath Mitalakar)

item.title: What a Webhook-Based Security Pipeline Can Catch That a Quarterly Audit Can't | VaultRak
item.description: A quarterly audit photographs your security posture at one moment. A webhook-based pipeline watches every change as it happens: vulnerable dependencies on the day they are pushed, config changes the afternoon they are merged, access grants the moment they land. The 90-day exposure window between quarterly audits is where most incidents begin and develop. VaultRak closes that window at the speed of the development team. On the live EncryptCoders engagement: 25 commits classified, 20 vulnerabilities remediated, 42 incidents resolved, 100% uptime. Built on Fortune 500 production expertise.
item.author: hr@t-matglobal.com (Sainath Mitalakar)

item.title: RBAC Drift: How Access Creeps Wider Over Time Without Anyone Noticing | VaultRak
item.description: RBAC drift is the silent accumulation of access that no single person approved. Temporary permissions that never expired, roles copied from broader templates, offboarding that missed a system, scope escalations nobody reverted. Together they produce an access surface wider than anyone intended. VaultRak monitors the access surface continuously so drift is caught before it becomes a breach vector. On the live EncryptCoders engagement: 25 security commits classified, 20 vulnerabilities remediated, 42 incidents resolved, 62/100 posture score. Built on Fortune 500 production expertise.
item.author: hr@t-matglobal.com (Sainath Mitalakar)

item.title: Why Most Startups Discover Security Gaps During a Customer Audit, Not Before | VaultRak
item.description: Most startups learn they have a security problem when a customer auditor asks for evidence they do not have. Remediation records, incident logs, access control documentation, and commit-level security classification are all standard audit requests that startups without ongoing security operations cannot produce from existing records. VaultRak builds audit-ready security posture continuously from day one of engagement. On the live EncryptCoders engagement: 62/100 posture score, 20 vulnerabilities remediated, 42 incidents resolved, 25 security commits classified. Built on Fortune 500 production expertise.

item.title: The Hidden Cost of Unreviewed Commits in a Fast-Moving Codebase | VaultRak
item.description: Every unreviewed commit is a window of undetected exposure. In fast-moving codebases, dependency additions, config changes, auth logic edits, and secrets handling refactors pass through code review without a security classification. VaultRak classifies every commit automatically via GitLab webhook at the speed of development. On the live EncryptCoders engagement: 25 security commits classified, 20 vulnerabilities remediated, zero commits left unreviewed. Built on Fortune 500 production expertise.

item.title: What a Security Score of 0 to 100 Actually Measures | VaultRak
item.description: A security posture score is not a compliance certification, not a CVSS average, and not a point-in-time snapshot. VaultRak's 0-to-100 score is a live composite of five signals: open vulnerability count and age, remediation velocity, incident resolution rate, pipeline coverage, and infrastructure compliance. The live client holds 62/100 — an honest number reflecting 20 vulnerabilities remediated, 42 incidents resolved, and zero findings left to age.
item.author: hr@t-matglobal.com (Sainath Mitalakar)

item.title: Vulnerability Scanning Is Not Remediation: Why Finding the Problem Is the Easy Part
item.description: Scanning for vulnerabilities and remediating them are two entirely different disciplines. Detection is automated and cheap. Remediation requires operating discipline: triage, ownership, fix verification, and posture maintenance over time. Most security programs accumulate findings and call it security. VaultRak turns findings into closed outcomes — 20 vulnerabilities remediated, 42 incidents resolved, 100% uptime. Built on Fortune 500 production expertise.
item.author: hr@t-matglobal.com (Sainath Mitalakar)
